author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected in place: its date and description change, the pet gains no additional visit, validated like booking, then the owner's record is shown. Reachable by its own address; no owner-page link in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Opening an existing visit's correction form shows the form prefilled with that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a present description and a date later than today updates the same visit in place, adds no additional visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record.
Submitting a blank description refuses the correction and names the description.
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the correction and names the date.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4)
A visible edit link from the owner detail page (deferred to a follow-up)
notes: NG-5 narrowed 2026-08-23 (adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md): correction in scope, cancellation out. Open question: whether the future-date rule applies when the visit's original date is now in the past — narrowest reading (same validation as creation) is in force; see PRD Open Questions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the established edit-in-place pattern (PetController.updatePetDetails, OwnerController edit) applied one level deeper in the Owner aggregate, exactly as the narrowing ADR (adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md) anticipated. The write goes through OwnerRepository.save(owner), the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph (system-design.md #contracts, Persistence). No new module, pattern, or integration; one bounded adjustment to VisitController's model-attribute loader is all that is new. Grep-confirmed against VisitController.java, PetController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java (no IDE oracle in this run; grep is the weaker basis).
integration_points: New GET+POST route pair /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController, reusing the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and the `visit` model attribute
Correction persists via OwnerRepository.save(owner) through JPA cascade on Pet.visits (@OneToMany CascadeType.ALL, @JoinColumn) — an UPDATE of the existing row, never an INSERT
system-design.md Contracts: VisitController/Visit/OwnerRepository rows updated to add REQ-VIS-003 and name in-place correction
docs/adr/README.md index: added the missing 2026-08-23 narrowing-ADR row (housekeeping the PRD expert could not do within its write scope)

patterns.description: updatePetDetails: load the existing child by id from the aggregate, mutate its fields via setters, saveAndFlush the root — the edit-in-place template to mirror for visits
getPet(Integer id): the id-lookup helper to mirror as a Pet.getVisit(Integer id) helper (none exists yet) for locating the visit to correct

risks.risk: The existing @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit unconditionally does `new Visit(); pet.addVisit(visit)`. Reusing it for the edit route would add a second visit (violating AC2 'the pet gains no additional visit') or bind onto the wrong object.
risks.mitigation: The edit flow must load the EXISTING Visit from pet.getVisits() by visitId (add a Pet.getVisit(Integer id) helper mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id), or iterate) and bind the form directly onto that managed instance, so owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE. Differentiate new-vs-edit in the loader (e.g. @PathVariable(required=false) Integer visitId) or use a separate model-attribute; do not share the new-visit population path.

risks.risk: A visitId not present among the pet's visits could NPE or silently mis-bind.
risks.mitigation: Reject an unknown visitId the same way the loader already rejects an unknown owner/pet — throw IllegalArgumentException. Parallels the existing 'booking for a pet not belonging to the owner is refused' edge case.

risks.risk: Tempting to relax the future-date rule so a visit whose original date is now in the past can be re-saved without moving its date.
risks.mitigation: PRD Open Question is settled to the narrowest reading: correction uses booking's validation unchanged (date must be after today). Reuse processNewVisitForm's exact check `!visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())` -> rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate') plus @Valid @NotBlank description. Do NOT special-case past original dates.

notes: Prefill (AC1) needs no template change: returning the existing visit as the `visit` attribute makes th:object bind visit.date/visit.description automatically; the template posts back to the current URL (method=post, no action) and its `visit['new']` guards render the 'Visit' heading and the previous-visits table correctly for an existing visit. The submit label #{addVisit} ('Add Visit') is cosmetic and not required by any AC — leave or relabel at implementer discretion. Keep the InitBinder setDisallowedFields('id','*.id') — the visit identity comes from the loaded entity, not the form (matches the identifier-tampering Threat Model row). Redirect on success to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}, as booking does. No orphan-removal concern: correction mutates, never removes. No ADR warranted — the edit-forward decision is already recorded in adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: review-plan-engine
rationale: risk triggers present (multi-module, oversize, design-revision); full battery

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Visit loader scopes the target strictly through the aggregate path (owner.findById -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId)); Pet.getVisit only searches that pet's own visit collection, so a visitId from another pet/owner is not found and raises IllegalArgumentException — no cross-aggregate IDOR

setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") retained on the binder; correction binds onto the existing managed Visit instance so the save cascades an in-place UPDATE with no identifier reassignment — mass-assignment/id tampering blocked
No injection surface: JPA repository (no SQL string-building), no file I/O (no path traversal), exception messages interpolate only typed int/Integer path variables
Future-date and @NotBlank validation applied identically to the booking flow before save

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) returns null when no visit is found. The checklist requires Optional for nullable return values. The caller in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit immediately null-checks and throws, which works but is less expressive than orElseThrow. The method mirrors the pre-existing Owner.getPet(Integer id) null-return pattern, but that precedent does not override the checklist for a new method introduced in this slice.
findings.fix: Change the return type to Optional<Visit>, replace the null return with Optional.empty(), and update the caller to pet.getVisit(visitId).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + petId + ".")).

approved_aspects: @ModelAttribute loader split on required=false visitId is the correct Spring MVC pattern for sharing a loader across new and edit flows
Error handling in loadPetWithVisit is consistent with the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found patterns (IllegalArgumentException with context)
processUpdateVisitForm faithfully mirrors processNewVisitForm: same date validation, same cascade-save via owner, same redirect
Four new tests cover all four REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criteria; data constants follow the meaningful-name convention
Test for in-place update correctly asserts visit count stays at 1, confirming no extra visit is inserted

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test covers the new error path introduced by this slice: a visitId that does not belong to the pet. Pet.getVisit() returns null (Pet.java line 97) and VisitController.loadPetWithVisit throws IllegalArgumentException (VisitController.java line 83). Both lines show missed coverage in JaCoCo. The design-block named this exact risk and named the mitigation (reject an unknown visitId the same way the loader rejects an unknown pet). The mitigation is implemented but untested. A test that GETs or POSTs /owners/1/pets/1/visits/99/edit where visitId 99 is not present on the pet should result in the controller throwing IllegalArgumentException, exercising both Pet.java:97 and VisitController.java:83.

All four new test methods were written after 2026-07-31 and must follow the project's BDD naming school: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. None do. Current names describe the action taken rather than stating what must be true afterward. Rename suggestions: 'theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBePrefillledWithCurrentDateAndDescription', 'theVisitShouldBeUpdatedInPlaceWithoutAddingAnotherVisitRecord', 'theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRejectedWhenDescriptionIsBlank', 'theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRejectedWhenDateIsNotInFuture'. The four pre-existing methods (lines 85, 92, 103, 113) were not touched in this diff and do not require renaming now per the brief.
findings.fix: Rename the four new test methods to follow the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach init() method was modified by this slice (visit setup was added) and now directly instantiates production types with new Owner(), new Pet(), and new Visit(). The brief (testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction) requires that tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward wrap construction in factory methods. All three constructor calls fall under this requirement because @BeforeEach was modified in this diff.
findings.fix: Introduce factory methods (e.g., createAnOwner(), createAPetWithId(int), createAVisit(int, LocalDate, String)) and replace the direct constructor calls in init() with those factories.

findings.description: The updateVisitInPlaceWithoutAddingAnotherVisitThenRedirectToOwner test extracts the single visit with pet.getVisits().iterator().next() rather than using AssertJ's singleElement() assertion. iterator().next() bypasses AssertJ's failure messages and hides the size contract already asserted on the prior line. assertThat(pet.getVisits()).singleElement() carries both the size check and element extraction in one chain.
findings.fix: Replace the hasSize(1) + iterator().next() pair with assertThat(pet.getVisits()).singleElement().satisfies(v -> { assertThat(v.getDate()).isEqualTo(correctedDate); assertThat(v.getDescription()).isEqualTo("Corrected description"); });

findings.description: rejectVisitCorrectionWithDateNotInFuture tests only today's date (the boundary value). The controller check !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()) also blocks past dates. A @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource covering today and a past date (e.g., yesterday) is more thorough and the brief calls for @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases. The equivalent new-visit test has the same gap — but that test was not modified in this diff so only the new test requires the change now.
findings.fix: Convert rejectVisitCorrectionWithDateNotInFuture to a @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource rows for today and at least one past date.

approved_aspects: Key behavioral guarantee is tested: updateVisitInPlaceWithoutAddingAnotherVisitThenRedirectToOwner checks pet.getVisits().hasSize(1) after a successful POST to the edit endpoint, confirming no additional visit record is added
All 8 tests (4 existing + 4 new) pass green
